description: A camera overlay with a rounded cut-out scan frame, rounded corner brackets, an optional scan line and an optional flashlight toggle.
overview:
`QRScanner` is a `View` that draws an overlay on top of whatever you pass as `children`, usually a camera preview. It does not open the camera itself. The overlay dims everything outside a square frame with rounded corners (drawn with `react-native-svg`) and marks the frame with four rounded corner brackets. When `scanLine` is set, a line moves up and down inside the frame with Reanimated while the state is `idle`.

The frame size defaults to 66% of the shorter side, capped at 260 points. It is centered horizontally and sits slightly above the vertical center. A `title` sits above the frame and a `description` below it; the flashlight button sits near the bottom edge.
usage:
Render your camera view as `children` and size the scanner with `className`. When there are no children, the background falls back to `bg-media`.

Set `state` to `success` or `error` after you read a code. The brackets fade to a matching color, `success` springs the frame slightly smaller and `error` shakes it. Pass `onTorchToggle` together with a controlled `torch` value to show the flashlight button; leave it out to hide the button. `title` and `description` accept strings or your own elements.

The `QRScannerState` type is also exported.

examples.Success: The `success` state with green brackets and a slightly smaller frame.
examples.ErrorState: The `error` state, which shakes the frame and turns the brackets red.
examples.WithoutTorch: A title and description with no flashlight button, because `onTorchToggle` is not passed.

QRScanner.state: `idle`, `success` or `error`. Sets the bracket color and triggers haptics, the success scale and the error shake. Defaults to `idle`.
QRScanner.title: Content shown above the frame. Strings are wrapped in a `Text`.
QRScanner.description: Content shown below the frame. Strings are wrapped in a `Text`.
QRScanner.scanLine: Shows the animated scan line while the state is `idle`. Defaults to `false`.
QRScanner.torch: Whether the flashlight is on. The button fills and the icon uses the fill weight when on. Defaults to `false`.
QRScanner.onTorchToggle: Called with the next torch value when the flashlight button is pressed. The button is shown only when this is set.
QRScanner.torchLabel: Accessibility label for the flashlight button. Defaults to `"Flashlight"`.
QRScanner.frameSize: Side length of the scan frame in points. Overrides the automatic size.

accessibility:
- The dimmed surround and brackets are hidden from VoiceOver and TalkBack.
- The overlay is a polite live region, so changes to the title and description are announced on Android.
- The flashlight button has the `button` role, uses `torchLabel` as its label and reports `torch` as its selected state.
- State changes to `success` and `error` play a matching haptic notification.
- The shake and scan-line animations respect the system reduce motion setting, and the success scale is skipped when reduce motion is on.
notes:
- Uses the `bg-media`, `text-scrim`, `text-on-media`, `text-success`, `text-danger` and `bg-accent` tokens; the flashlight button uses `bg-scrim` when off and `bg-on-media` with a `text-media` icon when on.
- The scan line restarts whenever the state returns to `idle`.
